title: Power Saw Safety
summary: Power saws cause thousands of serious injuries a year - shocks, cuts, and lacerations - and can kill. This talk covers blade and guard checks, kickback, entanglement, and electrical protection.
talking_points: Read the owner's manual before first use. Check that movable guards work. Keep blades sharp, clean, oiled, and free of cracks.
Wear goggles or safety glasses with side shields even under a face shield, and wear proper shoes.
Prevent entanglement: no jewelry or chains, no loose clothing, and tie long hair back inside your hard hat.
Cut only with a clear work area and solid footing. Check that the cutting path is free of nails and other objects, and set blade depth so it does not strike sawhorses or supports.

Kickback happens when the blade binds or pinches in the cut - the stock is not held on both sides, the offcut closes on the blade, the blade is dull or wrong for the material, or you force the cut. Prevent it: support the workpiece on both sides so the kerf cannot close, keep the upper and lower blade guards working, use a sharp blade rated for the material, let the blade reach full speed before you cut, never overreach, and stand to the side of the line of the cut - never directly behind the saw.
Make sure a corded electric saw is double-insulated with a 3-prong plug in a grounded outlet. Use a GFCI cord in damp conditions.
Let the blade spin down on its own - never stop it with your hand. Unplug the saw before changing a blade and keep control of the plug so no one else energizes it.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing, jammed, or tied-back blade guards
Dull, cracked, or dirty blades, or blade depth set to hit sawhorses or supports
Unsupported or pinching stock or offcut that can bind the blade, a missing or stuck lower blade guard, or dull, cracked, or wrong-type blades still in use
Nails, screws, or debris in the cutting path, or unstable footing or workpiece
Two-prong plugs, damaged cords, or no GFCI in damp areas
Loose clothing, chains, or untied hair near the blade
discussion_questions: How do you check the blade guard and blade before a cut?
What causes kickback, and how do you set up the cut to avoid it?
How do you make sure no one plugs the saw back in while you change the blade?
